title: Astrid and the Promise
premise: Odile Crane, a jaded wedding planner nursing a private betrayal, agrees to pose as the date of Astrid Vane—a vineyard heiress with a family reunion to survive—at a wedding she's coordinating. What begins as a transactional arrangement deepens as Astrid's family secrets surface: a forged will, an estranged brother, and the truth about the harvest that could save or ruin the estate. As Odile's professional loyalty to a client collides with her growing love for Astrid, she must choose between protecting a lie and exposing a truth that will shatter the family—and risk Astrid's forgiveness. They end the season together at the vineyard's first harvest, having forgiven themselves as much as each other.
about_author: Edmund Pemberton is the pen name of a former estate manager in the Loire Valley who spent a decade observing weddings, harvests, and the families they break and remake. He writes romance about people who arrive late to their own lives and find the door still open.

chapters.title: Terms of the Contract
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Burned out and cynical after a client's groom jilted her sister, Odile takes one last job: the Vane vineyard wedding. Astrid Vane corners her with an offer—pose as her date for the family reunion weekend in exchange for a fee Odile badly needs. Beat: wary transaction masking two people at the end of their ropes.

chapters.title: The Reunion Table
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The fake couple arrives at the estate and Astrid navigates her imperious grandmother, a hostile half-brother, and pointed questions about the will. Odile plays the role too well, deflecting a family blow-up with a planner's grace. Beat: unexpected gratitude—and the first crack in Astrid's armor.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Between toasts, Astrid and Odile slip away to the cellar and talk honestly for the first time—about Odile's sister, Astrid's dead father, the weddings Odile can no longer believe in. A near-kiss is interrupted by Astrid's brother Julien, drunk and accusatory. Beat: intimacy arrives before either consents to it.

chapters.title: The Second Signature
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid finds a second signature page in her father's will—one that transfers the vineyard's controlling shares to Julien, dated suspiciously. She suspects forgery but can't prove it, and telling the family risks everything. She almost tells Odile, then doesn't. Beat: the secret that will cost her the thing she's starting to want.

chapters.title: What the Client Pays For
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile discovers the same document while doing wedding logistics—and realizes her employer, the family lawyer, may have forged it. Her professional ethics demand silence; her feelings for Astrid demand truth. She stays quiet and hates herself for it. Beat: loyalty and truth begin their war in earnest.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The wedding proceeds beautifully—Odile's masterpiece—while the vineyard's first harvest waits on the vines. Astrid, watching Odile work, admits she's in love, and Julien, watching Odile too, realizes she knows something. He confronts Odile privately with a threat: stay silent or lose the fee and her reputation. Beat: love declared in the margins of a lie.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile recognizes Julien's coercion as the same cowardice that let her sister be humiliated while she stayed silent. In a raw solo scene she confronts her own reflection—her complicity, her cynicism, her belief that second chances are for other people. Beat: the forgiveness the blurb promises begins with herself.

chapters.title: The Toast That Breaks
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, with Odile's interlude. At the rehearsal dinner, Julien announces the will's terms publicly. Astrid, betrayed and humiliated, learns Odile knew and said nothing. She ends the fake engagement in front of everyone. Beat: the climax's emotional detonation—truth arriving as wreckage.

chapters.title: Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Refusing lawyers and lawsuits, Odile gathers the family in the cellar and lays out the evidence—the forged date, the lawyer's ledger, the ink—forcing a confession before the whole Vane clan. Julien, cornered, crumbles; the grandmother, shaken, restores Astrid's inheritance informally. Beat: justice delivered not by courts but by courage.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, closing with Odile's. Weeks later, the family picks the first harvest together, Julien given slow, earned redemption. Astrid finds Odile among the vines and asks her—not to fake a date, but to stay for real. Odile, believing in weddings again, says yes. Beat: forgiveness completed, second chance taken, love harvested.
